passage:
The following text is from an original short story.
Grandfather never praised my drawings. He would study each one for a long time, then point to a single line, the curve of a shoulder or the edge of a cloud, and say, "Again." For years I thought he was impossible to please. Only after he died did I find a folder in his desk: every drawing I had ever given him, each one dated in his careful hand.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: The narrator realizes that her grandfather valued her drawings far more than she had believed.
The narrator learns that her grandfather had once hoped to become a professional artist himself.
The narrator decides to stop drawing because she could never satisfy her demanding grandfather.
The narrator discovers that her grandfather had thrown away most of the drawings she gave him.
steps: For years the narrator believed her grandfather was impossible to please.
The folder of every drawing, each carefully dated, shows he treasured them.
So the story is about the narrator discovering how much he valued her work.
Nothing suggests he wanted to be an artist, that she quit, or that he discarded the drawings.
key: A final reveal in a story often changes the meaning of everything before it.
